newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine builders present Menem $27 bln program.
newsitem.headline: Argentine builders present Menem $27 bln program.

text.p: Argentina's construction industry chiefs presented to President Carlos Menem's cabinet Thursday their proposals for a $27 billion infrastructure program which they said could create 550,000 new jobs.

Francisco Macri, head of the industrial conglomerate Socma and representative of the Argentine Construction Chamber, told reporters after meeting Menem that the building program would count on public and private funds.

"We are proposing today with our project an investment of $27 billion over the next three years to create about 550,000 new jobs," said Macri, promising that the CAC would give further details at a news conference later Thursday.

Menem's Peronist government desperately needs good news on jobs ahead of key mid-term elections in Congress in October. Faced with roadblock protests by jobless people up and down the country, he has urged business to try to foment employment while making a halting attempt to modernize labor legislation.
Unemployment has more than doubled to 17.3 percent since Menem came to power in 1989. New job data are due July 18 but it is forecast unemployment will drop just one percentage point.

Earlier this week Menem announced plans to build 10,000 km of national highways, with $10 billion of investment which he said could create up to 30,000 new jobs. The government is studying funding it with price hikes on gasoline and diesel.
